html:
Intramuros, "within the walls", is the old walled city of Manila, founded by the Spanish in 1571. For over three centuries it was the seat of Spanish government in the Philippines and, for the Spanish, the whole of the city of Manila.

Miguel López de Legazpi took the site from the Muslim ruler Rajah Sulayman at the mouth of the Pasig River. Stone walls replaced wooden ones from the 1590s after Chinese pirate raids. Inside stood the governor's palace, the cathedral, monasteries, schools and the houses of Spaniards; Filipinos and the large Chinese merchant community lived outside the walls. Its wealth came from the Manila galleons.

Britain occupied it from 1762 to 1764 during the Seven Years' War. In 1898 the United States took the Philippines from Spain. In February 1945 the Battle of Manila between American and Japanese forces almost levelled it, and many civilians were killed. The San Agustin Church, from the early 1600s, was the main building to survive. Much of the walls and some buildings have since been restored.
